notes: Independent review dated 2026-11-07. checked counts discrete assertion checks, excluding URL reachability tests; the working checklist contains 118 entries. Checked all requested summary fields and seven numbers, fifteen core events (zero-based indices 0,2,4,5,9,10,12,13,14,15,16,18,19,21,22), the sole event quote, additional radio entries, all four perspectives, and the specified Earhart direction/menu content. Downloaded cited sources with curl, extracted PDFs using PyMuPDF, and rendered/read original scanned pages where embedded text was absent. The quote is verbatim. Checked UTC arithmetic uses Lae UTC+10 and Itasca UTC-11:30; the final rough-log call converts to 20:13 UTC. The later 20:25 report is appropriately identified as conflicting. Checked DMS and imperial-to-metric conversions are correct. The perspectives generally distinguish evidence, inference and advocacy fairly; the deaths are explicitly presumed elsewhere in the dataset. No passenger is named, and no gratuitous material was found. Earhart has no eventTimes override in direct.js. All 42 listed source URLs resolved to the intended source through curl or the web reader; no confirmed dead links. Curl initially returned 403 for s19/s41, but plain-curl retries succeeded. s31/s32 were readable with the web tool despite scripted 403s; s24/s42 returned HTTP-200 security-block pages to curl, so their actual articles were read with the web tool. s14 metadata/abstract resolved, but its linked full-text download redirected to a restricted login; the abstract supports the reported conclusion, and the original Hoodless report was separately read. Nauru details remain dependent on a documented archival transcription rather than the original station log/telegram. The Deep Sea Vision retraction was verified through the cited NPR report, not a directly retrieved company social-media post. The NDL catalog independently confirms 1935 publication; the complete book was not read. Research files were not changed.
